Clear, accessible privacy information and rights communications
nodes.summary: Every Article 13/14 notice and every Article 15-22 and 34 communication must be concise, transparent, intelligible, easily accessible and in plain language, especially when aimed at a child. It is given in writing or electronically, and orally only on request and once the person's identity is proven by other means.
nodes.quote: in a concise, transparent, intelligible and easily accessible form, using clear and plain language, in particular for any information addressed specifically to a child

nodes.label: Facilitate rights requests; no refusal in Art 11(2) cases unless identification impossible
nodes.summary: The controller must make it easy to exercise Articles 15-22 rights rather than obstruct them. Where its purposes do not need identification (Art 11), it may refuse only if it demonstrates it cannot identify the person, and the rights revive when the person supplies identifying information.
nodes.quote: The controller shall facilitate the exercise of data subject rights under Articles 15 to 22.

nodes.label: Respond within one month; extend only with timely notice and reasons
nodes.summary: Information on action taken on an Articles 15-22 request is due without undue delay and within one month of receipt, extendable by two further months only where complexity or number of requests makes it necessary and the subject is told of the extension and reasons within the first month. Electronic requests get electronic answers where possible unless the subject asks otherwise.
nodes.quote: without undue delay and in any event within one month of receipt of the request

nodes.label: Refusal notice with reasons and remedies
nodes.summary: When the controller does not act on a request it must tell the subject without delay, and at the latest within one month, why, and that they may complain to a supervisory authority and seek a judicial remedy.
nodes.quote: the reasons for not taking action and on the possibility of lodging a complaint with a supervisory authority and seeking a judicial remedy

nodes.label: Rights handling free of charge unless manifestly unfounded or excessive
nodes.summary: Notices, rights communications and actions are free; only for manifestly unfounded or excessive (notably repetitive) requests may the controller charge a reasonable administrative-cost fee or refuse. The controller carries the burden of demonstrating that character.
nodes.quote: any communication and any actions taken under Articles 15 to 22 and 34 shall be provided free of charge

nodes.label: Proportionate identity verification on reasonable doubt
nodes.summary: Only where there are reasonable doubts about who is making an Articles 15-21 request may the controller ask for more information, and only what is necessary to confirm identity. This is without prejudice to Article 11.
nodes.quote: the controller may request the provision of additional information necessary to confirm the identity of the data subject

nodes.label: Complete notice at direct collection
nodes.summary: When data are collected from the subject, the controller must at that moment give every applicable Article 13(1)-(2) item (identity, DPO, purposes and basis, legitimate interests, recipients, transfers, retention, rights, consent withdrawal, complaint, requirement/consequences, automated decisions). It is excused only insofar as the subject already has the information.
nodes.quote: at the time when personal data are obtained, provide the data subject with all of the following information

nodes.label: New-purpose notice before further processing
nodes.summary: Before processing data for a purpose other than the original one, the controller must inform the subject of the new purpose and relevant Article 13(2)/14(2) information. The same duty applies to indirectly obtained data under 14(4) (attached here because the inventory assigns 14(4) to no rule).
nodes.quote: prior to that further processing with information on that other purpose and with any relevant further information as referred to in paragraph 2

nodes.label: Complete notice for indirectly obtained data
nodes.summary: When data come from a source other than the subject, the controller must give every applicable Article 14(1)-(2) item, which unlike Article 13 includes the categories of data and the source (and whether it was publicly accessible).
nodes.quote: Where personal data have not been obtained from the data subject, the controller shall provide the data subject with the following information

nodes.label: Indirect-collection notice timing
nodes.summary: The Article 14 notice is due within a reasonable period and at the latest one month after obtaining the data, or earlier at the first communication with the subject or the first disclosure to another recipient, whichever comes first.
nodes.quote: within a reasonable period after obtaining the personal data, but at the latest within one month

nodes.label: Indirect-notice exceptions
nodes.summary: Article 14(1)-(4) notice may be skipped only insofar as the subject already has it, it is impossible/disproportionate or would seriously impair the processing (with protective measures such as public information), obtaining/disclosure is laid down by law, or professional secrecy applies. Exceptions (c) and (d) need Union or Member State law and so require an overlay.
nodes.quote: the provision of such information proves impossible or would involve a disproportionate effort

nodes.label: Demonstrable consent
nodes.summary: Where processing relies on consent, the controller must be able to prove that the data subject consented. The evidence must show a freely given, specific, informed and unambiguous affirmative indication (Article 4(11)).
nodes.quote: Where processing is based on consent, the controller shall be able to demonstrate that the data subject has consented

nodes.label: Distinguishable, intelligible consent request
nodes.summary: A consent request inside a written declaration covering other matters must be clearly distinguishable, intelligible, easily accessible and in plain language. Parts of the declaration that infringe the GDPR are not binding.
nodes.quote: the request for consent shall be presented in a manner which is clearly distinguishable from the other matters, in an intelligible and easily accessible form

nodes.label: Right to withdraw consent
nodes.summary: Data subjects may withdraw consent at any time, must be told so before consenting, and withdrawing must be as easy as consenting. Withdrawal does not make earlier consent-based processing unlawful.
nodes.quote: The data subject shall have the right to withdraw his or her consent at any time.

nodes.label: Consent not conditional on unnecessary processing
nodes.summary: In judging whether consent is freely given, utmost account is taken of whether a contract or service is made conditional on consent to processing not necessary for it. Such bundled consent should not be relied on.
nodes.quote: is conditional on consent to the processing of personal data that is not necessary for the performance of that contract

nodes.label: Child consent for information society services
nodes.summary: Where consent is the basis for offering an information society service directly to a child, the child's own consent suffices only from age 16, or a lower Member State age not below 13. Below that age consent must be given or authorised by the holder of parental responsibility.
nodes.quote: Where the child is below the age of 16 years, such processing shall be lawful only if and to the extent that consent is given

nodes.label: Verify parental authorisation
nodes.summary: When Article 8(1) requires parental consent, the controller must make reasonable efforts, considering available technology, to verify that the holder of parental responsibility gave or authorised it.
nodes.quote: The controller shall make reasonable efforts to verify in such cases that consent is given or authorised by the holder of parental responsibility

nodes.label: Special-category data prohibition and exceptions
nodes.summary: Processing Article 9(1) special-category data is prohibited unless an Article 9(2) exception is established. Exceptions (b), (g), (i) and (j) need a Union or Member State legal basis; (h) needs law or a contract with a health professional plus the 9(3) secrecy condition; Member States may add conditions for genetic, biometric and health data.
nodes.quote: data concerning health or data concerning a natural person's sex life or sexual orientation shall be prohibited

nodes.label: Professional secrecy for health and care processing
nodes.summary: Special-category data processed under the Article 9(2)(h) health and care exception must be processed by or under the responsibility of a professional, or another person, bound by secrecy under Union or Member State law or national competent-body rules.
nodes.quote: processed by or under the responsibility of a professional subject to the obligation of professional secrecy under Union or Member State law

nodes.label: Criminal convictions and offences data
nodes.summary: Data on criminal convictions, offences or related security measures may be processed on an Article 6(1) basis only under official-authority control or when Union or Member State law authorises it with appropriate safeguards. A comprehensive register of convictions may be kept only under official-authority control.
nodes.quote: shall be carried out only under the control of official authority or when the processing is authorised by Union or Member State law

nodes.label: Right of access: confirmation, data and processing metadata
nodes.summary: On request the controller must confirm whether it processes the requester's data and, if so, give access plus purposes, categories, recipients (esp. third-country), retention, rights, complaint right, source and automated-decision information, and the Article 46 safeguards for any transfer.
nodes.quote: confirmation as to whether or not personal data concerning him or her are being processed

nodes.label: Copy of data: first free, electronic form, protect others
nodes.summary: The controller provides a copy of the data, free the first time with only a reasonable administrative fee for further copies, in a commonly used electronic form for electronic requests unless asked otherwise. The copy must not adversely affect the rights and freedoms of others.
nodes.quote: The right to obtain a copy referred to in paragraph 3 shall not adversely affect the rights and freedoms of others.

nodes.label: Rectification and completion
nodes.summary: Inaccurate personal data must be rectified without undue delay on the subject's request, and incomplete data completed (including by a supplementary statement) having regard to the purposes of processing.
nodes.quote: The data subject shall have the right to obtain from the controller without undue delay the rectification of inaccurate personal data concerning him or her.

nodes.label: Erasure on a valid Article 17(1) ground
nodes.summary: The controller must erase without undue delay when any ground applies: no longer necessary, consent withdrawn with no other basis, successful Art 21(1) or any Art 21(2) objection, unlawful processing, legal obligation to erase, or data collected for an Art 8(1) information-society offer to a child.
nodes.quote: the controller shall have the obligation to erase personal data without undue delay where one of the following grounds applies

nodes.label: Retention despite erasure only on an Article 17(3) exception
nodes.summary: Erasure (and the 17(2) onward notice) is displaced only to the extent processing is necessary for expression/information, a legal obligation or public task, public health, Art 89(1) archiving/research/statistics, or legal claims. Ground (b) depends on Union/Member State law and needs an overlay; grounds (a) and (c) may need one depending on the Art 85 / Art 9(2)(h)-(i) basis relied on.
nodes.quote: Paragraphs 1 and 2 shall not apply to the extent that processing is necessary:

nodes.label: Inform other controllers when erasing data the controller made public
nodes.summary: If the controller made the data public and must erase them under 17(1), it must take reasonable steps, considering available technology and cost, to tell other controllers processing the data that the subject requested erasure of links, copies or replications.
nodes.quote: shall take reasonable steps, including technical measures, to inform controllers which are processing the personal data

nodes.label: Restrict processing on an Article 18(1) ground
nodes.summary: On the data subject's request, the controller must mark data as restricted when accuracy is contested, processing is unlawful but erasure is opposed, the data is needed by the subject for legal claims, or an Art 21(1) objection is pending verification.
nodes.quote: The data subject shall have the right to obtain from the controller restriction of processing where one of the following applies

nodes.label: Restricted data: storage only, other processing only on a stated exception
nodes.summary: Once restricted, data may be stored but otherwise processed only with the subject's consent, for legal claims, to protect another person's rights, or for important Union/Member State public interest.
nodes.quote: with the exception of storage, only be processed with the data subject's consent or for the establishment, exercise or defence of legal claims

nodes.label: Inform the subject before lifting a restriction
nodes.summary: A subject who obtained a restriction must be told by the controller before that restriction is lifted.
nodes.quote: shall be informed by the controller before the restriction of processing is lifted

nodes.label: Notify recipients of rectification, erasure or restriction; name recipients on request
nodes.summary: After a rectification, Art 17(1) erasure or restriction, the controller tells every recipient the data was disclosed to unless impossible or disproportionate. It must name those recipients to the subject on request.
nodes.quote: to each recipient to whom the personal data have been disclosed, unless this proves impossible or involves disproportionate effort

nodes.label: Provide portable data when the portability conditions hold
nodes.summary: Data the subject provided, processed by automated means on consent or contract, must be given to the subject in a structured, commonly used, machine-readable format. Portability does not by itself erase data and does not cover public-task processing.
nodes.quote: which he or she has provided to a controller, in a structured, commonly used and machine-readable format

nodes.label: Direct controller-to-controller transmission while protecting others
nodes.summary: On the subject's request, portable data is sent directly to another controller where technically feasible. Exercising portability must not adversely affect the rights and freedoms of others.
nodes.quote: the right to have the personal data transmitted directly from one controller to another, where technically feasible

nodes.label: Stop public-task or legitimate-interest processing after an objection unless overriding grounds
nodes.summary: When a subject objects on grounds of their particular situation to processing based on Art 6(1)(e) or (f), including profiling, the controller must stop. The exceptions are demonstrated compelling legitimate grounds that override the subject's interests, or legal claims.
nodes.quote: The controller shall no longer process the personal data unless the controller demonstrates compelling legitimate grounds for the processing

nodes.label: Stop direct marketing and related profiling on objection, with no override
nodes.summary: A subject may object at any time to direct marketing, including related profiling; the data must then no longer be processed for that purpose. No balancing or override is available.
nodes.quote: Where the data subject objects to processing for direct marketing purposes, the personal data shall no longer be processed for such purposes.

nodes.label: Present the objection right at first communication; automated and research objections
nodes.summary: The objection rights must be shown explicitly, clearly and separately no later than the first communication, and in information-society services may be exercised by automated technical means. For Art 89(1) research or statistics, the subject may object unless the processing is necessary for a public-interest task.
nodes.quote: shall be explicitly brought to the attention of the data subject and shall be presented clearly and separately from any other information

nodes.label: No solely automated decision with legal or similarly significant effects by default
nodes.summary: A subject must not be subjected to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling, that has legal or similarly significant effects, unless an Art 22(2) exception applies.
nodes.quote: the right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling, which produces legal effects concerning him or her

nodes.label: Use an automated-decision exception only with its condition and safeguards
nodes.summary: Solely automated significant decisions are permitted only when necessary for a contract, authorised by law with safeguards, or based on explicit consent. For the contract and consent cases the controller must offer at least human intervention, a chance to give a view, and a way to contest.
nodes.quote: the right to obtain human intervention on the part of the controller, to express his or her point of view and to contest the decision

nodes.label: No special-category data in automated decisions unless Art 9(2)(a)/(g) and safeguards
nodes.summary: Excepted automated decisions must not rely on special-category data unless explicit consent (9(2)(a)) or a substantial-public-interest law (9(2)(g)) applies and suitable safeguards are in place.
nodes.quote: shall not be based on special categories of personal data referred to in Article 9(1), unless point (a) or (g) of Article 9(2) applies

nodes.label: Risk-appropriate measures and demonstrable compliance
nodes.summary: The controller must implement technical and organisational measures (including data protection policies where proportionate) suited to the processing and its risks, be able to demonstrate compliance, and review and update the measures where necessary. Codes of conduct or certification are only an element of that demonstration.
nodes.quote: shall implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure and to be able to demonstrate that processing is performed in accordance with this Regulation

nodes.label: Data protection by design
nodes.summary: When determining the means of processing and during processing, the controller must build in measures such as pseudonymisation that implement data-protection principles effectively and integrate the necessary safeguards, taking account of state of the art, cost, context and risk.
nodes.quote: implement appropriate technical and organisational measures, such as pseudonymisation, which are designed to implement data-protection principles, such as data minimisation, in an effective manner

nodes.label: Data protection by default
nodes.summary: Default settings must limit the amount of data collected, the extent of processing, the storage period and accessibility to what each specific purpose requires. By default, personal data must not be made accessible to an indefinite number of people without the individual's intervention.
nodes.quote: by default, only personal data which are necessary for each specific purpose of the processing are processed

nodes.label: Joint-controller arrangement and rights against each controller
nodes.summary: Joint controllers must transparently allocate their responsibilities (notably rights handling and Article 13/14 information) in an arrangement, unless and in so far as law determines them, and make its essence available to data subjects. Data subjects may exercise their rights against each joint controller regardless of the arrangement.
nodes.quote: They shall in a transparent manner determine their respective responsibilities for compliance with the obligations under this Regulation

nodes.label: EU representative for non-established controllers and processors
nodes.summary: A controller or processor not established in the Union whose processing falls under Article 3(2) must designate in writing a representative established in a Member State where the relevant data subjects are. It does not apply to occasional, unlikely-to-be-risky processing without large-scale special-category or criminal-offence data, or to public authorities or bodies.
nodes.quote: Where Article 3(2) applies, the controller or the processor shall designate in writing a representative in the Union.

nodes.label: Processor selection and written processing contract
nodes.summary: A controller may use only processors that provide sufficient guarantees, and only under a binding written (including electronic) contract or legal act that sets out the processing particulars and every Article 28(3)(a)-(h) term. Codes, certification and standard contractual clauses can support this but do not replace it.
nodes.quote: the controller shall use only processors providing sufficient guarantees to implement appropriate technical and organisational measures

nodes.label: Sub-processor authorisation and flow-down obligations
nodes.summary: A processor may engage another processor only with the controller's prior specific or general written authorisation; under a general authorisation it must inform the controller of intended additions or replacements so the controller can object. The same data-protection obligations must be imposed on the sub-processor by contract, and the initial processor remains fully liable for it.
nodes.quote: The processor shall not engage another processor without prior specific or general written authorisation of the controller.

nodes.label: Processing only on documented instructions
nodes.summary: The processor and anyone acting under the authority of the controller or processor may process personal data only on the controller's documented instructions, including for third-country transfers, unless Union or Member State law requires it, in which case the processor informs the controller first unless that law forbids this. Authorised persons must be bound to confidentiality, and Article 32 measures and sub-processor conditions must be respected.
nodes.quote: processes the personal data only on documented instructions from the controller, including with regard to transfers of personal data to a third country

nodes.label: Processor assistance to the controller
nodes.summary: Taking into account the nature of processing and the information it has, the processor must assist the controller, insofar as possible, in responding to data-subject rights requests and in meeting Article 32-36 obligations. The obligation to respond to the data subject remains the controller's.
nodes.quote: assists the controller in ensuring compliance with the obligations pursuant to Articles 32 to 36 taking into account the nature of processing

nodes.label: End-of-service return or deletion, audits and infringing-instruction alerts
nodes.summary: At the end of the services the processor must, at the controller's choice, return or delete all personal data and delete existing copies unless Union or Member State law requires storage, and must make compliance information available and allow audits by the controller or its mandated auditor. It must immediately inform the controller if it considers an instruction infringes data-protection law.
nodes.quote: at the choice of the controller, deletes or returns all the personal data to the controller after the end of the provision of services

nodes.label: Records of processing activities
nodes.summary: Each controller (and its representative) must keep a written record of processing activities containing all Article 30(1) fields; each processor keeps a record of categories of processing carried out for each controller with the Article 30(2) fields. Electronic form is allowed.
nodes.quote: shall maintain a record of processing activities under its responsibility. That record shall contain all of the following information

nodes.label: Record production and small-organisation exception
nodes.summary: The record must be made available to the supervisory authority on request. Organisations employing fewer than 250 persons are exempt from keeping it only if their processing is not likely to result in a risk, is occasional, and includes no special-category or criminal-offence data.
nodes.quote: shall make the record available to the supervisory authority on request

nodes.label: Cooperation with the supervisory authority
nodes.summary: Controllers, processors and, where applicable, their representatives must cooperate with the supervisory authority, on request, in the performance of its tasks.
nodes.quote: shall cooperate, on request, with the supervisory authority in the performance of its tasks

nodes.label: Art 22(1)/(4) automated decision-making, including profiling, is used on the subject's data
nodes.quote: the existence of automated decision-making, including profiling, referred to in Article 22(1) and (4)

nodes.label: The controller is not taking (all or part of) the action requested
nodes.quote: If the controller does not take action on the request of the data subject

aliases.label: The controller is not taking action on the subject's rights request

nodes.label: Personal data are being collected directly from the data subject
nodes.quote: Where personal data relating to a data subject are collected from the data subject

nodes.label: The data came from publicly accessible sources
nodes.quote: whether it came from publicly accessible sources

nodes.label: Personal data were obtained from a source other than the data subject
nodes.quote: Where personal data have not been obtained from the data subject

nodes.label: Indirectly obtained data are to be used to communicate with the subject
nodes.quote: if the personal data are to be used for communication with the data subject

nodes.label: Disclosure of indirectly obtained data to another recipient is envisaged
nodes.quote: if a disclosure to another recipient is envisaged, at the latest when the personal data are first disclosed

nodes.label: The controller has documented evidence demonstrating the manifestly unfounded/excessive character
nodes.quote: The controller shall bear the burden of demonstrating the manifestly unfounded or excessive character of the request.

nodes.label: Subject was told of the extension and its reasons within one month of receipt
nodes.quote: inform the data subject of any such extension within one month of receipt of the request, together with the reasons for the delay

nodes.label: Controller intends to process the data for a purpose other than the original collection purpose
nodes.quote: Where the controller intends to further process the personal data for a purpose other than that for which the personal data were collected

nodes.label: Requester's identity is already established by the controller's existing means (e.g. authenticated account session)
nodes.quote: where the controller has reasonable doubts concerning the identity

nodes.label: The requester's identity has been proven by means other than the oral exchange itself
nodes.quote: provided that the identity of the data subject is proven by other means

nodes.label: Controller has reasonable doubts about the requester's identity
nodes.quote: where the controller has reasonable doubts concerning the identity of the natural person making the request

nodes.label: Giving the Art 14 notice proves impossible or would involve disproportionate effort
nodes.quote: the provision of such information proves impossible or would involve a disproportionate effort

nodes.label: Giving the notice would render impossible or seriously impair the processing's objectives
nodes.quote: is likely to render impossible or seriously impair the achievement of the objectives of that processing

nodes.label: Obtaining or disclosure is expressly laid down by Union/Member State law with protective measures (overlay)
nodes.quote: obtaining or disclosure is expressly laid down by Union or Member State law to which the controller is subject

nodes.label: One month has already passed since the request was received
nodes.quote: in any event within one month of receipt of the request

nodes.label: One month has passed since the indirectly obtained data were obtained
nodes.quote: but at the latest within one month

nodes.label: The data subject asks for the information to be given orally
nodes.quote: When requested by the data subject, the information may be provided orally

nodes.label: Processing relies on Art 6(1)(f) legitimate interests (notice must state them)
nodes.quote: where the processing is based on point (f) of Article 6(1), the legitimate interests pursued by the controller or by a third party

nodes.label: Data must stay confidential under a professional secrecy obligation regulated by law (overlay)
nodes.quote: the personal data must remain confidential subject to an obligation of professional secrecy regulated by Union or Member State law

nodes.label: A less intrusive check using data the controller already holds would suffice to confirm identity
nodes.quote: additional information necessary to confirm the identity of the data subject

nodes.label: Appropriate protective measures (e.g. information made publicly available) are in place when notice is skipped
nodes.quote: the controller shall take appropriate measures to protect the data subject's rights and freedoms and legitimate interests, including making the information publicly available

nodes.label: Providing the data is a statutory or contractual requirement or needed to enter a contract
nodes.quote: whether the provision of personal data is a statutory or contractual requirement, or a requirement necessary to enter into a contract

nodes.label: Controller has an EU representative (identity/contact must appear in notices)
nodes.quote: where applicable, of the controller's representative

nodes.label: The request is complex or the subject has made a number of requests, making extra time necessary
nodes.quote: taking into account the complexity and number of the requests

nodes.label: The request was made by electronic means
nodes.quote: Where the data subject makes the request by electronic form means

nodes.label: The request is manifestly unfounded or excessive
nodes.quote: Where requests from a data subject are manifestly unfounded or excessive

nodes.label: A rights request arrives through a channel or wording other than the controller's designated request form
nodes.quote: The controller shall facilitate the exercise of data subject rights under Articles 15 to 22.

nodes.label: The subject's requests are repetitive
nodes.quote: in particular because of their repetitive character

nodes.label: Processing is for public-interest archiving, scientific/historical research or statistics under Art 89(1) safeguards
nodes.quote: subject to the conditions and safeguards referred to in Article 89(1)

nodes.label: The data subject already has the notice information
nodes.quote: shall not apply where and insofar as the data subject already has the information

nodes.label: The subject asked for the response in a different form than the electronic default
nodes.quote: unless otherwise requested by the data subject

nodes.label: Union/Member State law authorises the processing and provides appropriate safeguards
nodes.quote: authorised by Union or Member State law providing for appropriate safeguards for the rights and freedoms of data subjects

nodes.label: Biometric data are processed to uniquely identify a person (e.g. face-matching login)
nodes.quote: biometric data for the purpose of uniquely identifying a natural person

nodes.label: The child is below the applicable Article 8 age (16, or the Member State age, not below 13)
nodes.quote: Where the child is below the age of 16 years

aliases.label: The child is at or above the applicable age threshold (16, or a lower Member State age not below 13)

nodes.label: The processing would create or keep a comprehensive register of criminal convictions
nodes.quote: Any comprehensive register of criminal convictions shall be kept only under the control of official authority

nodes.label: Contract or service is made conditional on consent to processing not necessary for it
nodes.quote: When assessing whether consent is freely given, utmost account shall be taken

nodes.label: No record demonstrates that this data subject consented (who, when, to what wording)
nodes.quote: the controller shall be able to demonstrate that the data subject has consented

nodes.label: Consent is sought within a written declaration that also concerns other matters (e.g. terms and conditions)
nodes.quote: consent is given in the context of a written declaration which also concerns other matters

nodes.label: The recorded 'consent' is not a statement or clear affirmative action (e.g. default-ticked box, silence)
nodes.quote: by a statement or by a clear affirmative action, signifies agreement

nodes.label: The consent request is not clearly distinguishable, intelligible, easily accessible or in plain language
nodes.quote: the request for consent shall be presented in a manner which is clearly distinguishable from the other matters, in an intelligible and easily accessible form

nodes.label: The data subject has withdrawn consent on which processing was based
nodes.quote: the data subject withdraws consent on which the processing is based

nodes.label: Processing involves data on criminal convictions, offences or related security measures
nodes.quote: personal data relating to criminal convictions and offences or related security measures

aliases.label: The processing includes special-category or criminal-conviction data (defeats 30(5))

nodes.label: A not-for-profit body would disclose the data outside the body without the data subjects' consent
nodes.quote: the personal data are not disclosed outside that body without the consent of the data subjects

nodes.label: Necessary for archiving/research/statistics per Article 89(1) based on Union/Member State law (9(2)(j))
nodes.quote: necessary for archiving purposes in the public interest, scientific or historical research purposes or statistical purposes in accordance with Article 89(1)

nodes.label: Necessary for employment/social-security/social-protection obligations or rights, as authorised by law or collective agreement (9(2)(b))
nodes.quote: in the field of employment and social security and social protection law in so far as it is authorised by Union or Member State law

nodes.label: Data subject gave explicit consent for one or more specified purposes (9(2)(a))
nodes.quote: the data subject has given explicit consent to the processing of those personal data for one or more specified purposes

aliases.label: The subject gave explicit consent to use the special-category data for the specified purpose
The processing is based on consent (6(1)(a) or 9(2)(a)) or contract (6(1)(b))

nodes.label: Necessary for preventive/occupational medicine, diagnosis, health or social care or treatment, on law or a contract with a health professional (9(2)(h))
nodes.quote: the provision of health or social care or treatment or the management of health or social care systems and services

nodes.label: The data were manifestly made public by the data subject themselves (9(2)(e))
nodes.quote: processing relates to personal data which are manifestly made public by the data subject

nodes.label: Purpose limitation
nodes.summary: Collect personal data only for specified, explicit and legitimate purposes and do not further process them incompatibly. Further processing for public-interest archiving, research or statistics under Article 89(1) is deemed not incompatible.

nodes.label: Data minimisation
nodes.summary: Data must be adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary for the purpose. Collecting, retrieving or using fields beyond that need is non-compliant.
nodes.quote: adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary in relation to the purposes for which they are processed

nodes.label: Accuracy
nodes.summary: Keep personal data accurate and, where necessary, up to date. Take every reasonable step to erase or rectify data that are inaccurate for their purpose without delay.

nodes.label: Storage limitation
nodes.summary: Keep data in identifiable form no longer than the purpose requires. Longer storage is permitted only for archiving, research or statistical purposes with Article 89(1) safeguards.
nodes.quote: kept in a form which permits identification of data subjects for no longer than is necessary for the purposes

nodes.label: Integrity and confidentiality
nodes.summary: Process data with appropriate security, protecting against unauthorised or unlawful processing and accidental loss, destruction or damage. Disclosures and destructive operations must be authorised and secure.

nodes.label: Accountability: demonstrable compliance

nodes.label: Processing requires a lawful basis
nodes.summary: Processing is lawful only if, and to the extent that, one of the six Article 6(1) bases applies; bases (c) and (e) must be laid down in Union or Member State law. Legitimate interests fail where overridden by the data subject's interests or rights (especially a child's) and are unavailable to public authorities performing their tasks.

nodes.label: Further-processing compatibility test

nodes.label: Processing that does not require identification

nodes.label: Mandatory DPIA categories
nodes.summary: A DPIA is always required for systematic and extensive automated evaluation on which significant decisions are based, for large-scale special-category or criminal-offence data, and for large-scale systematic monitoring of publicly accessible areas.

nodes.summary: Where a DPO is designated, the controller must seek the DPO's advice while carrying out the DPIA. The DPIA must at least describe the processing and purposes, assess necessity, proportionality and risks, and set out the measures to address them.

nodes.summary: Controllers and processors must designate a DPO when they are public bodies (other than courts acting judicially) or when their core activities involve large-scale regular and systematic monitoring or large-scale special-category and criminal-offence data. nodes.label: Position and independence of the DPO
nodes.summary: The controller and processor must involve the DPO properly and in time, provide resources and access, let data subjects contact the DPO, and have the DPO report to the highest management level. nodes.summary: The DPO must at least inform and advise, monitor compliance, advise on and monitor DPIAs, cooperate with the supervisory authority and act as its contact point, giving due regard to processing risk.

nodes.label: Breach notification to the supervisory authority
nodes.summary: On a personal data breach the controller must notify the competent supervisory authority without undue delay and, where feasible, within 72 hours of becoming aware, unless the breach is unlikely to result in a risk to natural persons. nodes.label: Transfers subject to appropriate safeguards

open_questions.question: Article 8(1) applies only 'where point (a) of Article 6(1) applies'; how should a child's use of an information society service on the contract basis be treated? Article 8(3) defers to Member State contract law (overlay), so no path was written.

Whether a plain photo, or special-category data inferred from other data (e.g. health inferred from purchases), counts as Article 9(1) data turns on 'revealing' and on Article 4(14) 'specific technical processing'; only the face-matching (unique identification) case is pathed.
Article 37(1)(c) says special categories 'and' criminal-offence data, while Article 35(3)(b) and Article 30(5) say 'or'; the RA-06 edge is annotated but the literal reading is unresolved.

DP.PF-04.04 treats verifying contested accuracy before rectifying as a reasonable step (5(1)(d), 18(1)(a)); Article 16 grants rectification 'without undue delay', so the DR fragment's position should be checked for consistency.

Whether a commercial NDA can make an IT contractor 'another person also subject to an obligation of secrecy' under 9(3) depends on Union/Member State law or competent-body rules; DP.CS-08.03 escalates instead of deciding.
Article 11(2) disapplies Articles 15-20 only, so Article 21 objections still apply to data the controller cannot identify; how an objection is executed in that case is not addressed by the text.
The schema has no edge type for 'factor weighed' (rule to state condition), so the Article 6(4)(a)-(e) factor nodes are reached only through decision paths.

Shared conditions such as consent withdrawal or 'no lawful basis' may also be minted by the DR or CM fragments (e.g. K.DR.consent_withdrawn); merging should deduplicate them against K.CS.consent_withdrawn and K.PF.no_lawful_basis.

12(3): does 'number of the requests' mean only requests from the same subject, or can controller-wide request volume (backlog) justify the two-month extension? Paths assume only the subject's own requests or the request's complexity count.

12(3)/12(6): the text does not say whether the one-month clock pauses while the controller waits for identity information requested under 12(6). Paths treat 'not until verified' as DENY and avoid timing claims for that interval.

12(5) is permissive ('may either'): fulfilling a manifestly unfounded or excessive request stays lawful. DENY and fee paths therefore need the scenario to record the controller's chosen option. 'Manifestly unfounded' has no textual test beyond the repetitive example, so motive-based cases are routed to ESCALATE.
15(4) textually limits the copy right in 15(3). Whether it also limits 15(1)(g) source information when the source is an identifiable person is unresolved; modelled as ESCALATE (DP.DR-02.04).

Requests made through representatives (a lawyer, family member, or parent for a child) are not regulated by Arts 12-17; Art 80 covers only not-for-profit bodies. Paths model only 'no evidence of authority'; a scenario with a parent or agent needs an overlay or design decision.
14(4) (new-purpose notice for indirectly obtained data) has no rule in rule_inventory.md. It is attached to CM-08 here; the CM-11 override of CM-08 applies only to that 14(4) part.

17(1)(c) second limb: the text does not say whether a 21(2) marketing objection supports erasure of all the subject's data or only data processed for marketing. DP.DR-04.04 avoids the question by using a subject whose only remaining data is the marketing profile.

17(1)(e), 17(3)(a)-(c) and 14(5)(c)-(d) depend on Union or Member State law. Those paths are marked overlay_required, and scenarios must carry the specific statute (e.g. a retention-schedule entry citing it).

17(2) 'reasonable steps ... taking account of available technology and the cost' sets no threshold, and it is unclear whether unknown downstream controllers must be traced. Paths use only identifiable controllers with available removal channels.
12(1): what counts as identity 'proven by other means' for oral information is not defined. Paths use a channel authentication (one-time code) as proof.
13(4)/14(5)(a) apply 'insofar as' the subject already has the information. Partial possession (some fields known, others changed) is not modelled; paths assume complete or no prior information.

Art 19 notification covers erasure 'in accordance with Article 17(1)' but not the 17(2) notice to other controllers; DR-06 and DR-10 are therefore modelled as separate duties with different addressees (controllers vs recipients).

Art 18(1)(b) vs 17(1)(d): it is unclear whether a subject's choice of restriction over erasure displaces the controller's own obligation to erase unlawfully processed data. Modelled as tension_with DR-04, with restriction as the path outcome.

Art 18(1) is a right the subject must 'obtain' (request), yet 21(1) says processing stops unless grounds are demonstrated. Whether the controller must restrict automatically on any 21(1) objection, or only when asked, is not stated. DP.DR-13.02 restricts proactively.

Art 18(1)(a)/(d) give no time limit for the verification period, and Arts 18/21 set no deadline for the restriction or stop itself. Timing is modelled via 12(3) (without undue delay / one month), which strictly governs 'information on action taken'.

Art 19 covers erasure 'in accordance with Article 17(1)' only. Whether erasure for other reasons (e.g., routine retention expiry, or erasure under 17(2)) also triggers recipient notification is not stated.

Art 19 'impossible or disproportionate effort' has no criteria in the text, and the recipient-list duty has no explicit deadline beyond 12(3). Disproportionate-effort judgments are modelled as ESCALATE to the DPO.

Art 4(9) excludes public authorities receiving data in a particular inquiry from 'recipients'. Whether such entries must be withheld from the Art 19 recipient list depends on the governing Union/Member State law (overlay).
Art 20(1) 'provided by' the subject: the text clearly excludes controller-computed inferences. Whether observed data (activity logs, telemetry) counts as 'provided' is not settled by the text.
Art 20(3)'s public-task exclusion largely overlaps 20(1)(a), since public-task processing is not consent or contract. It is kept as a separate exception node.
Art 20(4) 'shall not adversely affect the rights and freedoms of others' gives no method. Redaction is modelled for clear co-holder data, and ESCALATE for bulk third-party datasets.
Art 21(1) does not say who decides, or by what test, whether 'compelling legitimate grounds' override. It is modelled as a DPO decision; an operational agent should not self-certify it.
Art 21(5) names no technical specification, so which machine-readable opt-out signals count as a valid objection is not determinable from the text.
Art 21(6) together with Art 89(2): Member State law may derogate from Art 21 for research. No such overlay is assumed; DP.DR-15.04 assumes none exists.
Art 22(1) 'solely' and 'similarly significantly affects' are undefined. Token or rubber-stamp human review is modelled as ESCALATE (DP.DR-16.04) because the text does not resolve it.
Art 22(2)(a) 'necessary' for a contract has no test. Paths assert necessity as a scenario fact rather than deriving it.
Art 22(4): whether decisions using proxies or inferences for special-category data (e.g., inferred health status) are 'based on' Art 9(1) data is not addressed.
Art 22(4) via 9(2)(a): explicit consent may be unavailable where Union or Member State law says the prohibition cannot be lifted. DP.DR-18.02 assumes no such law.

Art 80(1) covers lodging complaints and Arts 77-79/82 remedies. It does not say whether a mandated body may exercise Arts 15-22 rights for the subject, or how a controller verifies a mandate. DP.OL-03.03 and DP.OL-03.04 assume disclosure needs separate verification and controller sign-off.

Art 23: a supplied measure may also restrict Art 12(4) refusal reasons and remedy notices (Art 23 covers Art 12). The communication content in restricted cases therefore depends entirely on the overlay text.
Art 78(2) gives the supervisory authority a three-month progress-reporting duty. It binds the authority, not the controller, so no controller deadline node was created.

Art 33(1)/(2): the text starts the controller's 72 hours when the controller 'becomes aware' and requires the processor to notify without undue delay, but does not say whether a processor's awareness is imputed to the controller; scenarios should state when the controller itself learned of the breach.

Art 28(3) second subparagraph: the processor must immediately inform the controller of an instruction it considers infringing, but the text does not say whether it must suspend execution meanwhile. DP.GP-10.06 is labelled ESCALATE (not executed by the agent) and forbids the disclosure because it would independently breach Art 9; confirm this convention.
Art 28(2): the consequence of a controller's objection to a sub-processor change under general authorisation is not spelled out; DP.GP-07.05 treats the objection as blocking the engagement (DENY).

Art 28(3)(e) and Art 29: the text puts the duty to respond to rights requests on the controller and limits the processor to assisting and to processing on instructions, but it does not explicitly say 'forward the request'. DP.GP-09.02 marks the hand-off as gdpr_text; it could be argued to be role_authority.

Art 30(5): unclear from the text whether 'occasional', 'likely to result in a risk' and the special-category or criminal-data disqualifiers are assessed per processing activity or across all of the organisation's processing ('the processing it carries out'), and 'occasional' is undefined. Scenarios should state the facts so that only one reading applies.

Art 26: when Union or Member State law determines the joint controllers' responsibilities (so no arrangement is needed 'in so far as' the law covers them), the text does not say whether the 26(2) duty to make the arrangement's essence available still applies.

Arts 33(1)/34(1): 'unlikely to result in a risk' and 'high risk' are not defined in the text; every breach path must state the risk-assessment outcome as a scenario fact rather than leaving the agent to infer the threshold.

Schema: obligated_party takes one ID, but Arts 27, 30, 31, 32(1) and 32(4) bind both controller and processor. GP-05, GP-11, GP-12, GP-13, SB-01 and SB-02 list C.controller and carry applies_to C.processor edges; the merger may want a list-valued field instead.

Verification of a supervisory-authority request (DP.GP-12.01, DP.GP-13.02) is not covered by the GDPR text; the escalation of an unverified request to the DPO is grounded only in role authority and the Art 39(1)(d)-(e) contact-point task.

Art 36(1) literally says consult where the DPIA shows high risk 'in the absence of measures taken by the controller to mitigate the risk'; read alone this could cover every high-risk DPIA. Recitals 84 and 94 support the residual-risk reading (risk the controller cannot mitigate). K.RA.residual_high_risk_unmitigated follows the recitals.

Art 36(2) does not say whether processing may start while the supervisory authority's up-to-8(+6)-week period is still running without a reply (Recital 94 only says silence is without prejudice to later intervention). DP.RA-05.05 models this as ESCALATE (role_authority) with no forbidden action.

Art 37(1)(c) in the English text reads special categories 'and' criminal-offence data (conjunctive). Whether large-scale special-category data alone triggers a DPO is not settled by the text; no path relies on that reading.

'Large scale', 'core activities' (only Recital 97 helps), 'systematic monitoring' and 'likely to result in a high risk' are not defined in the text. Scenarios must state these as facts or route the question (DP.RA-02.05).

The GDPR does not define 'transfer' (e.g. remote access from a third country, or sending data to an importer that is itself subject to the GDPR under Art 3(2)). Scenarios should state explicitly that a transfer occurs.
Art 38(6) does not say which other tasks create a conflict of interests. Scenarios must state the conflict as a fact (DP.RA-07.03); no role is assumed to conflict.

Recital 111 describes contract and legal-claims transfers as 'occasional', but Art 49(1)(b),(c),(e) do not say so. Paths use one-off transfers; whether repeated transfers under (b)/(c)/(e) are allowed is left open.

Art 46(1) requires 'enforceable data subject rights and effective legal remedies' to be available but gives no method for checking third-country law. DP.XT-03.05 escalates instead of inventing an assessment standard.

The SA lists under 35(4)/(5) are authority-issued content that the environment must carry as state. The text does not say what happens if an operation on a no-DPIA list also shows high-risk indicators.
Art 48 plus Art 6(3): disclosure under an MLAT also needs a lawful basis, and a 6(1)(c) basis must be laid down in Union or Member State law. DP.XT-05.03 is marked overlay_required.
OL-04 scope: the schema's scope list does not name Articles 82-84. It is set to 'conditional' because it needs a court or authority role; Art 84 penalties are Member State law.
The text does not say whether Article 49(1)(a) 'explicit consent' must also meet the Art 4(11)/7 consent conditions (CS-01..CS-03), so no edge was added between XT-06 and CS-*.
T.prior_to_processing is proposed as a new deadline ID, because the shared vocabulary has no deadline for the 'prior to processing' timing in 35(1) and 36(1).
